entries.name: Ashglass Volcanoes
entries.summary: A far southeastern volcanic region of black beaches, lava-lit islands, fire-glass cliffs, ash gardens, obsidian roads, sulfur channels, ruined docks, sealed prisons, and fortified cities built around heat and stone. Ashfall, red night-glow, and brittle black ground make travel beautiful, dangerous, and hard on animals and gear. Citizens, ash sailors, contract guards, miners, wardens, cult hunters, refugees, and stranger volcanic creatures move between safe roads and forbidden scars.

entries.name: Blackbell Deadroads
entries.summary: A northern deadland of abandoned villages, black grass, plague pits, broken bell towers, sunken grave tracks, and ruined watchroads between living territories. Cold wind moves through empty streets, and old snow gathers where doors have not opened in years. Warden patrols, scavengers, desperate refugees, curse hunters, and restless dead make the roads feel occupied even when no army holds them.

entries.name: Blackroad Borderlands
entries.summary: A hard eastern borderland of military roads, dry hills, fortified estates, border watches, labor routes, garrisons, census posts, and contested crossings. Dust, heat, and road discipline shape the landscape, while mountains and open ground leave few routes unseen. Soldiers, farmers, clerks, laborers, scouts, refugees, smugglers, and frontier families live under visible pressure from rival authorities.

entries.name: Crownlake Heartlands
entries.summary: The central lake-and-bay heartland of river mouths, ferries, palace roads, harbor towns, market crossings, academic compounds, guild quarters, embassies, docks, and crowded approach roads. Water, traffic, bells, and road dust make the region busy in every season, though fog and rain can slow even official travel. Courtiers, dockworkers, students, guards, merchants, servants, travelers, and common households crowd the land around the capital routes.

entries.name: Dawnwater Shorelands
entries.summary: An eastern shoreland of river mouths, island channels, cold-water harbors, naval posts, watch towers, clan crossings, sea-facing towns, and long roads that end at docks. Mists rise from the channels in the morning, and storms can turn a governor road into a waiting room for ships. Sailors, fishers, officers, ferrymen, clan households, customs clerks, and coastal traders live by tide tables and river law.

entries.name: Deepforge Highlands
entries.summary: A northeastern highland of forge roads, high passes, mineral ridges, storm harbors, coastal holds, deep stone settlements, and old routes into cold northern waters. The land is steep, rocky, and rich beneath the surface, with rain on the lower coasts and snow along the upper roads. Miners, smiths, caravan guards, stonecutters, harbor crews, tunnel scouts, and mountain patrols keep to durable roads and defensible halls.

entries.name: Drowned Green Coast
entries.summary: A wet southwestern coast of drowned woods, reed mouths, stilt hamlets, blackwater ferries, hidden causeways, fog banks, and green hills sinking into channels. Rain, tide, peat water, and root-choked inlets shift the road from season to season. Ferrymen, fishers, herb gatherers, marsh guides, smugglers, troll hunters, and wary village families know paths that look like water to outsiders.

entries.name: Elderwood Crownwoods
entries.summary: A great western forest heartland of canopy roads, old boundary trees, river clearings, noble groves, hidden watch paths, and halls built around living trunks rather than against them. The air stays green and dim under deep leaves, and even maintained paths feel watched by age and memory. Forest households, guides, wardens, hunters, scholars, exiles, and long-settled grove communities inhabit the clearings and river bends.

entries.name: Frostpine Gatewoods
entries.summary: A cold border forest of dark pines, snow-fed valleys, old cart tracks, stone watchposts, and high passes rising toward the northern glacier mountains. Winter lingers in shaded gullies, and the roads grow quiet where roots, snow, and old markers cross. Sparse woodland settlements, guides, patrol shelters, and guarded crossings serve travelers who know how easily the forest turns them around.

entries.name: Galechain High Isles
entries.summary: A far sea-torn island reach of high green cliffs, broken reefs, beacon rocks, fishing harbors, wreck coves, and narrow storm roads between scattered settlements. Hard rain, sudden fog, and hidden channels make local pilots more important than straight maps. Fishing families, harbor crews, shrine keepers, smugglers, and wreck salvagers live where the cliffs leave room for docks.

entries.name: Great Greenwild
entries.summary: A vast green interior of ancient forest, mossy hills, river bends, hidden clearings, beast paths, old standing stones, and herbalist tracks under heavy canopy. Warm rains, deep shade, and shifting animal trails make the wilds feel larger than the map allows. Hunters, guides, witches, beastkin families, hermits, woodcutters, monsters, and small hidden settlements survive by reading signs outsiders miss.

entries.name: Greenvale Heartlands
entries.summary: A broad central heartland of farm valleys, green roads, river towns, fortified bridges, abbey lands, old quarries, mill streams, and noble estates. The climate is temperate and workable, with muddy springs, full summer fields, and road traffic that rises after harvest. Farmers, reeves, roadwardens, monks, merchants, quarry crews, and local guards make the region settled but still vulnerable to ordinary trouble.

entries.name: Highwind Escarpments
entries.summary: A high eastern region of cliff cities, storm bridges, wind roads, snow peaks, lift platforms, griffin eyries, rope stations, and ledges where one broken span can isolate a village. Weather changes by height, with clear lower roads giving way to hard gusts, lightning, and thin cold air above. Climbers, sky sailors, bridge crews, herders, engineers, monks, and mountain guards live by landing rights and safe passage.

entries.name: Ledgerbay Harbors
entries.summary: A central-southern harbor belt of sheltered ports, warehouses, toll houses, ferry markets, convoy yards, debtor docks, and sea roads feeding inland trade routes. Warm rain, gull noise, ship lanterns, and stacked cargo make the waterfronts busy even before dawn. Dockworkers, brokers, sailors, customs clerks, guards, smugglers, debtors, and traveling merchants fill the streets between wharves and counting houses.

entries.name: Pearlwater Lagoons
entries.summary: A far southern lagoon-and-reef region of coral halls, tide markets, sea caves, pylon towns, shallow courts, submerged ways, pearl houses, and passages reachable only at certain tides. Warm water, bright shallows, slow currents, and moonlit sandbars make movement beautiful but exacting. Pearl workers, harbor pilots, sea elves, merfolk envoys, reef guards, traders, and tide-law interpreters live where land and water share authority.

entries.name: Runehall Pine Coast
entries.summary: A western mainland coast of pine ridges, cold rivers, timber halls, stone law-courts, beacon towers, fortified river towns, hill forts, ancestral barrows, and saga-marked boundary stones. Rain, sea wind, and long grey light give the coast a hard northern edge even in settled provinces. Fishers, woodcutters, road guards, household warriors, judges, oath witnesses, raiders, and farmers share land where every crossing has a memory.

entries.name: Sapphire Outer Reefs
entries.summary: A far southwestern reef reach of turquoise shallows, shipwreck teeth, pearl channels, reef roads, sea caves, fishing islets, and harbors that appear safe only from a distance. Water clarity hides rocks, currents, and predators until a pilot knows the color of each channel. Fishers, pearl divers, wreck salvagers, island traders, pirates, reef guides, and tide-watchers occupy the safer coves and outer platforms.

entries.name: Shadowglass Headlands
entries.summary: A far northeastern headland of dark coves, snow-shadowed ridges, cliff keeps, black-water villages, old baron roads, and cold sea approaches. The coast is sharp, wind-bitten, and often overcast, with lanterns showing from windows long before a traveler sees a safe harbor. Fishing hamlets, fortified estates, watch posts, coastal guides, and night-travelers live under a mood of guarded hospitality.

entries.name: Stormbreak Reefroads
entries.summary: A western island-and-sea lane of reef keeps, scattered ports, smuggler coves, fishing villages, storm harbors, and dangerous blue channels. Squalls move fast over shallow water, and reefs turn calm sailing into careful navigation by soundings, birds, and local memory. Island crews, pilots, traders, smugglers, storm-priests, and harbor militias crowd the few reliable landings.

entries.name: Stormcarved Skerries
entries.summary: A lower western island belt of jagged skerries, pine-shadowed coves, raider landings, beacon rocks, fishing halls, narrow sounds, and old sea roads. Salt wind, sudden rain, and broken stone make the shoreline difficult to read from offshore. Fishers, beacon keepers, coastal defenders, raiders, smugglers, and island families occupy the coves that can hold a hall or a hidden boat.

entries.name: Sunroad Coast
entries.summary: A southeastern pilgrim coast of hot roads, shrine harbors, dry hills, protected wells, monastery approaches, sea cliffs, salt flats, and watched crossings toward ash-sea routes. Sun glare, dust, and sea wind dominate travel, while evening cool brings movement back to the roads. Pilgrims, monks, healers, well guards, merchants, patrols, fishermen, and hidden cult agents pass through the same harbors and roadside shelters.

entries.name: Sunspine Pilgrimlands
entries.summary: A southern sacred dryland of sun-baked ridges, white roads, monastery fields, reliquary paths, guarded wells, healing houses, ash courts, shrine towns, and long pilgrim routes. Heat, bright stone, dry wind, and sudden night cold make travel physically demanding even on maintained roads. Pilgrims, monks, healers, temple guards, farmers near wells, relic keepers, merchants, and suspicious strangers share crowded route towns.

entries.name: Thundergrass Steppe
entries.summary: A broad grassland of open horizons, fortified wells, storm-black skies, shrine stones, herd trails, seasonal camps, low ridges, and long roads worn by hooves. Thunderheads roll across the plains fast, and distance is measured by water, shelter, and who controls the next well. Roaming clans, beastkin families, orcish holds, ogre pact-bands, traders, scouts, monster herds, and war camps move with the seasons.

entries.name: Whitecrown Glacier Range
entries.summary: A severe far-northern belt of white peaks, glaciers, frozen lakes, buried roads, wind-cut valleys, and barrow-stones half-swallowed by ice. Weather can close a pass in an hour, and distance feels longer under glare, snowmelt, and thin mountain air. Miners, wardens, hardy road crews, shrine tenders, giants, and stranger old things occupy the valleys and ruined high routes.

entries.name: Wolfroad Marches
entries.summary: A southern marchland of dry hills, broken roads, fortified wells, clan camps, mercenary posts, contested passes, ruined watchtowers, and border markets. Heat, dust, and thin grazing make every caravan route depend on water, escort, and reputation. Mercenaries, caravan crews, clan exiles, scouts, traders, bandits, shepherds, and ruined-town survivors gather where the roads remain passable.
